surfaces.part: mirror head (round disc seen face-on, with a sky and ground reflection and an orange frame)

answer.evidence: The head spans rows 0-13 and its width profile is 8, 10, 11, 13, 15, 13, 11, 9, 7, then 5 for the shaft. The silhouette is therefore round and bounded by narrower rows above and below. The interior is a vertical mirror face: x=8 shows rows 4-7 as blue sky, row 8 as a green horizon line and rows 9-11 as a pale ground reflection. This is a face-on disc, not a horizontal plate seen from above, so I see no front-edge line, eave shadow or contents that would mark a top surface. The shaft in rows 14-27 is a 5px vertical strip with a light side and a dark side. The base in rows 28-31 is a small plate 8-10px wide with a light top row at x=5 and darker rows below, which makes it a narrow foot. Overall this is a front elevation: a round, overhanging head that has no top surface.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a thin pole prop with a round mirror head. Its measured facts are at or above the thin references: 24 distinct colours against 14 for the lamp and bench, and a median of 20 colours per tile against 10-20 for the hedge, stall and well. Flat-fill coverage is 0%. Dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline carries a tint (brownish rim, bluish-grey pole) and is not a sticker-style black line. By eye the mirror disc has a rim, a bright glass highlight and a darker lower glass tone, and the pole has light and dark sides. That gives roughly 4-5 steps per material, comparable to the lamp-crook. It is small and simple, but it does not look thinner or flatter than the references, so a careful artist would accept it next to them.

surfaces.part: mirror head (round disc on a pole)

answer.evidence: The head is a face-on circle. The width profile widens from 8 to 15 (rows 0-8) and narrows to 7 (row 13), then the shaft is 5 wide (rows 14-27). So the silhouette is round at both edges and overhangs the shaft. The interior shows a vertical mirror face with a sky-blue gradient, a green horizon band at row 8 and a grey lower reflection, framed by an orange/yellow ring. There is no foreshortened top plate, no front-edge line and no eave shadow, so the disc is a vertical face, not a horizontal cap. The shaft is a plain vertical strip (x=5 brown, x=8 red-brown stripes, x=12 dark). The base at rows 28-31 is only 4 rows tall, with a light row 29, and is a minor detail.

styleAnswer.evidence: The measured facts favour the candidate. It has 20 distinct colours per full tile, level with prop-well-roofed (20) and above prop-hedge (10). Flat-fill coverage is 0%, and 0% of its dark edge pixels are near-neutral, so the outline carries a colour tint. Unlike the lamp-crook's neutral black line, it is not the sticker look. By eye, the round mirror has a frame ring with highlight and shadow sides, a graded glass face with a glint, and a shaded pole and base, about 5 lightness steps. That is close to the references. Its 24 total colours are lower than the stall and well (38-40) but above the bench, hedge and lamp (11-14), which is fair for a small, thin single-tile prop. Texture is modest rather than rich, since there is no grain on the pole or base. Even so, a careful artist would accept it next to the references without it looking flatter or thinner.
